html:
An epidemic of smallpox that broke out among the Aboriginal people around Sydney in April 1789, about 15 months after the First Fleet arrived. It killed perhaps half of the local Eora people.

British officers found bodies in caves and on beaches around the harbour. The colonists themselves were almost untouched. Where the disease came from is still argued: some historians point to dried smallpox matter the fleet's surgeons carried for inoculation, others to Makassan fishermen who visited northern Australia. The Aboriginal man Arabanoo, who had been captured by the colonists, died of it while nursing the sick.

The loss broke the power of local clans to resist the settlement in its first years. Bennelong, one of the survivors, became a go between with the British. The epidemic was one of many in which European diseases cleared the way for colonisation. It is a turning point in the history of Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: An epidemic of smallpox that broke out among the Aboriginal people around Sydney in April 1789, about 15 months after the First Fleet arrived. It killed perhaps half of the local Eora people.
